description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 after a cold review of the absorption prototype (BLOCK).

WHAT WAS BUILT AND WHY IT IS WRONG: Types::rung_absorbs(hi, lo, mask) folding
a list(none)-keyed recursive activation into the standing list(τ) one at
IGNORE positions only, on the argument that empty_list() at an ignored
position proves every contributing row held []. That argument is true and
irrelevant: it says nothing about whether the LO rows and the HI rows belong
to ONE CALLER. The key erases an ignored callable slot to a2, so two users
with different reducers are indistinguishable there and the rung is the only
position that separates them. Attack b1 (review-attacks/b1_same_driver_diff_
acc.fz): an [int]-driven Enum.reduce with [] acc -> [int], then [] acc ->
[binary]; base and E' publish `([binary] | [int])` (the sound fz-kdt.189
over-approximation); absorption publishes `([int])` -- UNSOUND -- and with
the two statements swapped it is green: ORDER-DEPENDENT, on all three doors.
DispatchDemand::Ignore means clause selection never ASKS about the position,
not that the body never READS it: an accumulator at an Ignore position IS
the return, so merging keys that differ only there merges returns. The
corpus already carries the configuration (List.reduce_while_cont/3[list(int),
{empty_list(), int}, a2]). The own-ascent conjunct (absorb only into an
activation whose PRECISE rows already cover this call) closes b1/b2 but
panics under fz-kdt.120's rule -- a diagnostic, not a landing.

THE RETIREMENT DESIGN (a per-function activation-key antichain fact) was
judged against the engine's laws and does not survive as stated: the
absorber search inside canonical_activation_key is an UNLEDGERED read of
mutable world state (the cause of the 3 schedule movers, the 3 public_trace
uncaused-evaluation failures and the order dependence); an insert-and-evict
antichain is monotone only in its DOWN-SET; the unclaimed-activation path
re-lists claims and does NOT delete the executable (fz-kdt.69's decommission
is the unnamed hard prerequisite -- why the "forwarding" variant died with
"no backend entry clause matched for executable 22"); the fact can only be
read-with-subscription, never waited (circular producer/waiter), so the first
mint reads Absent and the ladder is STILL minted -- "deletes the transient
work" is false by construction.

THE POPULATION IS 183's TO DEFINE, AND ITS RULE DELETES IT: under "element
precision only where demand reaches the element through forwarding"
(list.fz:46-56) reduce_cont/3's accumulator is consumed only by reducer.(head,
acc) (key a2, not ground) and {:done, acc} (a construction) -> FREIGHT;
reduce_step/3's {:cont, acc} field forwards to freight; reduce_while_cont/3,
List.reverse/2, partition/4's accumulators -> freight. Only reduce_step/3's
LIST slot (forwarded to reduce_cont/3, ground in the element) is demanded.
64 of the 173 E'-created rungs sit on those five freight positions; no rung
the rule keeps was found. The earlier headline gate (partition/4 with a
GROUND element) contradicted the rule: under it the accumulators stay
list(a2_e) = HEAD, already one key. Note also E' ALONE was schedule-
confluent (FIFO/LIFO movers 0); absorption made it 3.

THE CENSUS (kept as fact): distinct emitted keys, empty ⊑ list(τ) only,
rejecting empty/non_empty pairs: 53 pairs over 15 fixtures at HEAD, of which
30 compile identical code and 23 differ -- but "differs" does not attribute
to the rung: count/1 is an honest specialization (slot 0 is its dispatch
position); Enumerable.Range.reduce/3's difference is blind callable evidence
(fz-kdt.189) and its returns are INVERTED (the wider key returns the
narrower type). A ratchet must attribute the difference to the rung slot.

WHAT REMAINS OF THIS TICKET: after fz-kdt.183's rule lands, re-run the rung
census against it and state the surviving population with named functions.
If empty, CLOSE this ticket as retired by 183 with the measurement. If a
population survives, a fold needs (a) a law that names the ASCENT (one
caller's own ladder), not just the position, (b) fz-kdt.69's decommission as
a declared blocker, (c) the frontier fact as a down-set join read with
subscription, (d) a red-first anti-blend gate: b1 publishes `([binary] |
[int])` in BOTH statement orders. BLOCKED BY fz-kdt.183.

comments.text: Data point from fz-kdt.132 (c31b309d0), which this ticket was named as a neighbour of. The take_drop 'cross-key subsumption smell' this ticket's neighbourhood was suspected of was NOT subsumption: the three same-function accumulator keys ({[], []}, {[], [int]}, {[], [int]} | {[int], []}) were a truncated ASCENT LADDER, not redundant siblings. Deduping them by containment would have been the wrong cure -- the right one minted the rung above them and the ladder collapsed to a single key on its own (three reducer specializations per captured lambda became one, 00420 215 -> 196 executables). Worth re-measuring 00277's Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] vs Kernel.dbg/1[list(int)] pair against HEAD before building: the population this ticket asks to count may have moved.

RE-MEASURED at d2a5f3510 (2026-09-02), head FIFO vs head LIFO: the Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] + fz_dbg_value/1[empty_list()] pair exists under LIFO only (beside dbg/1[list(int)] on both), and BOTH return `any` -- the fz-kdt.120 defect (a @spec variable bound to the whole `[]` argument is dropped by arrow_match.rs's empty-list ambiguity rule, so `dbg(t) :: t` at `[]` loses its result). FIFO carries its own one-schedule key instead: Range.reduce/5[..., {:cont, empty_list()}, ...]. So the population this ticket asks to count is, at head, two `[]`-keyed activations that a schedule mints when a callsite's argument is `[]` at an intermediate round and that survive beside the wider key. Sequence: after fz-kdt.120's rule lands (the `[]`-keyed dbg will then return `[]`, not `any`), re-count; what remains is the minting question this ticket owns, and fz-kdt.132's lesson applies (a truncated ascent ladder is not a subsumption problem).

CLOSED AS REFUTED / SUPERSEDED (2026-09-03, owner decision): key-level empty-rung absorption blends two users that differ only in a []-seeded accumulator (attack b1/b2: an unsound, order-dependent published return on three doors), and the activation-key antichain design is unsound and contrary to exact, ledgered dependencies (an unledgered read of mutable world state inside the key mint; an insert-and-evict join that is not monotone as a set; a fact that can only be read, never waited; fz-kdt.69's decommission as an unnamed prerequisite). fz-kdt.183's demand-through-forwarding rule never mints the ladder this ticket would fold; its post-change rung census (rungs_canon.py definition, base 53/15, must not grow, created rungs named) is now 183's acceptance item. The HEAD population of 53 rungs stays: they sit on non-recursive keys where the key is evidence.

title: Empty-rung absorption at the key level is BLOCKED and likely retired: it blends two users that differ only in a []-seeded accumulator, and fz-kdt.183's demand-through-forwarding rule never mints the ladder it would fold
